progressionSystems.detail: Four ranks: Starter (default/unranked start), Great Rank, Ultra Rank, Master Rank. Rank rises automatically by completing 'Important Requests' and story milestones (tied to meeting Legendary Pokémon), not by an XP/grind system. Great Rank unlocks Bleak Beach and Rocky Ridges; Ultra Rank unlocks Sparkling Skylands; Master Rank has no further area unlock and is obtained during Sparkling Skylands after examining the Master Ball, marking rough completion of the main story.
progressionSystems.trackable: No dedicated menu/meter. Rank-ups are announced via a game-paused notification (Pokédex tells you the new rank), usually after a Legendary cutscene. Otherwise the only way to 'check' rank is to test a locked green area gate to see if it opens.

progressionSystems.detail: A per-region development score reflecting habitat variety, decoration, vegetation, housing quality, Pokémon comfort, and population. There are 5 towns total: 4 story regions (Withered Wasteland, Bleak Beach, Rocky Ridges, Sparkling Skylands) plus one sandbox town, Palette Town, which reportedly does not have a story-gated Environment Level in the same way.
progressionSystems.trackable: Community sources state Environment Level is viewable/trackable per-region, though exact UI location not independently confirmed (NintendoLife guide page returned 403 and could not be verified directly).

progressionSystems.detail: Reaching Environment Level 5 in each region is stated by one source as required to reach the credits/ending; a separate claim states maxing every region to Environment Level 10 is required for '100% completion.' Rebuilding a region's Pokémon Center requires Environment Level 3, a 1,000 Life Coin Rebuilding Kit, and 8 qualifying Pokémon for that area; rebuilding all 4 main-story Pokémon Centers is required to reach the credits.
progressionSystems.trackable: low confirmation on exact max level number (5 vs 10 conflicting between sources) — needs verification.

progressionSystems.detail: Separate from Friendship. Measures how a specific Pokémon feels about its habitat/surroundings. Rises faster when the Pokémon likes you (friendship); in turn friendship rises faster when Comfort is high. Two systems are parallel/per-individual-Pokémon, not a single global stat.
progressionSystems.trackable: Unconfirmed whether displayed as a numeric value or only a qualitative indicator in the Pokémon's info screen.

progressionSystems.detail: Raised by completing a Pokémon's requested task, giving favorite items, playing minigames ('Look This Way', quizzes), or spending time near them. Milestones: Pokémon starts seeking the player out and leaving gift materials mid-tier; at max friendship a Pokémon calls the player by their chosen name (instead of 'Ditto') and explicitly announces being your best friend.
progressionSystems.trackable: Behavioral/qualitative signals confirmed (naming change, gift-dropping, best-friend dialogue) but no confirmed numeric friendship meter shown in a menu.

progressionSystems.detail: Main currency, used at the Pokémon Center PC shop for furniture, recipes, seeds, and kits (e.g., recipe packs cost 500–5,000 Life Coins). Earned mainly via 'Challenges' completed at the PC.
progressionSystems.trackable: Life Coin total presumably shown in PC shop/wallet UI (not independently screenshotted/confirmed by scout).

progressionSystems.detail: Over 600 crafting recipes across six categories, unlocked via story progression, exploration rewards, shop purchases, and Pokémon friendships. Materials gathered by cutting wood, breaking rocks, exploring, etc.
progressionSystems.trackable: Unconfirmed whether the game shows a 'recipes learned / total' counter.

progressionSystems.detail: Pokémon don't roam the overworld randomly — they appear at player-built 'habitats' (specific item arrangements). Each habitat can host one Pokémon at a time. Count of distinct habitats cited inconsistently across sources: one tracker site claims '214 Habitats', another claims '212+ habitats'.
progressionSystems.trackable: unconfirmed exact number; treat as approximate ('~212-214') pending official confirmation.

progressionSystems.detail: Small and Large Lost Relics can be given to Professor Tangrowth's 'Appraise' specialty for a random reward (Habitat recipe, item recipe, or usable item). Community count: 37 Large Relics and 46 Small Relics (83 total) — single-source figure, unverified officially. Gimmighoul trading also exists: trading an appraised relic, Rainbow Feather, or Silver Feather to Gimmighoul yields one random rare furniture item.
progressionSystems.trackable: Unconfirmed whether a relic-collection checklist/counter exists in-game.

progressionSystems.detail: Supports Link Play multiplayer in Palette Town or on Cloud Islands. Dream Islands are accessed by befriending Drifloon, completing its habitat, and obtaining a doll; different dolls lead to different Dream Islands. Multiplayer session rules: all players must agree to travel to/leave a Dream Island together. Requires Nintendo Switch Online + internet.
progressionSystems.trackable: n/a for solo trophies unless a specific multiplayer trophy is desired; flagging as a system that could gate an online-required objective.

trackableStats.where: In-game Pokédex accessible via menu; multiple third-party trackers mirror it (PokoTraqr, Pokopia Companion) implying the base game has a Pokédex with caught/seen states.

Community sources state 300 numbered entries in the base Pokédex, with a total of ~304 including event Pokémon; a separate Pokédex exists for Expansion Pass (Bubbly Basin) additions. Exact base-game number needs official confirmation before being used as a hard trophy target.
No persistent menu meter; shown only via one-time rank-up notification popup and by testing area gates.
Reportedly viewable per-region; exact UI location and max value (5 vs 10, sources conflict) not independently confirmed.
Presumed shown in PC/shop UI; not independently confirmed by this scout.
Likely visible on individual Pokémon info screens, but scout could not confirm whether shown as a number, bar, or only qualitative behavior cues.
Unconfirmed whether an in-game counter exists despite 600+ total recipes being documented by third parties.
Unconfirmed whether an in-game checklist exists; only fan trackers (RankedBoost) maintain lists.
Version 2.0.0 patch notes state photo display limit increased from 10 to 40, implying a photo gallery/storage screen exists.

missables.detail: Chosen once at the start and cannot be changed afterward (appearance/cosmetics ARE changeable via mirrors, but the name is permanent).
All playthroughs begin on the same starting island/tutorial layout; cannot be altered or re-chosen.

Community claim: some Pokémon and cosmetic items (e.g., 'Sprout Festival Petals' in spring, 'Sun-Crested Hat' in summer, 'Harvest Festival Charm' in autumn, 'Frost Sprite Pendant' in winter) appear only during a specific in-game season (~30 in-game days per season). Missing the window means waiting roughly a full year to retry on the same save. NOTE: exact item names come from a single fan-guide source (pokopia.center) that reads as possibly AI-generated/unverified boilerplate — treat these specific names with caution.

missables.item: Real-time limited events / Mystery Gift codes
missables.detail: Pokopia runs real-time-dated events (similar to Animal Crossing) offering exclusive Pokémon or items only obtainable while the event is live. Mystery Gift codes are one-time per save; most seasonal event content is stated to return the following year, but Mystery Gift codes reportedly do not return once expired.
Talking to certain NPCs for the first time in a specific window gives a one-time item; once the dialogue changes, the reward is permanently gone for that save.

missables.item: Pre-Legendary dialogue/cosmetic unlocks in Sparkling Skylands
missables.detail: Community claim that certain cosmetic dialogue rewards tied to each Legendary Pokémon encounter vanish permanently once that Legendary is caught/befriended.

rngSystems.detail: Pokémon appear at built habitats rather than roaming freely. Each habitat has a filtered pool of possible Pokémon based on habitat type, time of day (Morning 5-10AM, Daytime 10AM-5PM, Evening 5-8PM, Night 8PM-5AM, or 'All day'), and weather. Rarity affects spawn speed: Common appears within minutes, Uncommon takes longer, Rare requires more patience/waiting.

Weather changes dynamically in-game (unlike time of day, which follows the real-world clock) and affects which Pokémon can appear at habitats. Players can force certain weather via specific habitat structures (e.g., a Rain Dance Site habitat triggers rain; a Sunny Day Site forces sun).

CONFLICTING information. Most sources/community consensus (including a Pokémon.com official forum thread) state Pokopia does NOT have traditional shiny Pokémon, partly because its 'one Pokémon of each species befriended' design removes the repeat-encounter loop that shiny hunting relies on. One single fan guide claims a 1-in-500 (0.2%) shiny rate exists via wild encounters. This is a load-bearing discrepancy — do NOT build a shiny-hunting trophy without further official confirmation.
Giving a Small or Large Lost Relic to Professor Tangrowth's Appraise specialty yields a random reward (a habitat recipe, item recipe, or usable item) — outcome cannot be predicted/chosen.
Trading an appraised relic, a Rainbow Feather, or a Silver Feather to Gimmighoul returns one random rare furniture item.

versionDifferences.note: Switch 2 exclusive — no other hardware platform release exists to diff against as of August 2026.

Version 2.0.0 (released August 5, 2026, free update) added the Dive move (build underwater; requires knowing Surf and completing the 'Raise the environment level!' request at Bleak Beach), plus underwater Build specialty, new items (portal pod, safe), Dynamic Ditto print pattern, 5 new hair colors, bulk item transfer, item deletion from storage containers, motion-sickness camera settings, automatic re-habitation of rebuilt structures, batch relic appraisal (up to 10 at once), power generator placement cap raised to 128, and photo display limit raised from 10 to 40. This is a significant content/QoL update that post-dates original March 5, 2026 launch — any trophy list should account for whether it targets pre- or post-2.0.0 game state.

Expansion Pass (paid DLC) Part 1, 'Bubbly Basin,' released August 5, 2026 alongside the 2.0.0 free update. Adds a fully underwater settlement area, an additional Dream Island, buoyant/floating-building blocks, new furniture, and (per pre-launch reveals) at minimum the Popplio, Mudkip, and Corphish evolution lines plus Manaphy as new attractable Pokémon. Full new-Pokémon roster for this DLC was not fully enumerated in available sources. This is paid, optional content — any trophies referencing it should be flagged as DLC-dependent, not base-game.

Expansion Pass is planned to release in three parts total (Part 1 'Bubbly Basin' out August 5, 2026); Parts 2 and 3 were not yet released as of this research (August 12, 2026) — confirm release status before finalizing any DLC-based trophies.

Prior patch history (pre-2.0.0): v1.0.1 (Mar 4, 2026, activated online features), v1.0.2 (Mar 4, 2026, quest fixes + Spinarak type correction), v1.0.3 (Apr 9, 2026, search/navigation/construction/habitat fixes), v1.0.4 (Apr 23, 2026, enabled Pokémon Center relocation during special events), v1.1.0 (Jun 9, 2026, enabled Expansion Pass purchasing + Dynamic Ditto Print items), v1.1.1 (Jun 19, 2026, minor item-placement and photo-mode fixes). None of these appear to have removed content, only fixed bugs and added minor features — no evidence of cut content between versions.
No region-specific (Japan vs. US/other) content or achievement differences were found in available sources. Game appears to be a simultaneous worldwide release with identical content.
